sections.h2: Which office files deeds for Oakland County land?
sections.html:
The county Clerk/Register of Deeds files them. Questions about land records go to 248-858-0597 or deeds@oaklandcountymi.gov, and the counter serves visitors on weekdays, opening at 8:30 in the morning and closing at half past four. Almost 100 employees work in the combined office, which serves roughly 1.2 million residents and ranks among the biggest in Michigan.

Oakland County dates to 1820, and the office keeps documents from that period. Michigan counties rarely merge the two offices, but Oakland did so in 1958. Staff record more than 140,000 real estate documents every year.

The county has 530,460 households and 569,537 housing units. About nine in ten residents (89.1%) stayed at the same address through the prior year, per the Census Bureau, and monthly owner costs have a median of $1,998 with a mortgage and $778 without. Mortgages and discharges therefore pass through the recording counter next to deeds.

The public record spans deeds, mortgages, foreclosure records and personal property filings. Online copies reach back to January 1, 1964 through the Oakland County Super Index, with subdivision plats excluded. As of November 3, 2025 the office stopped recording UCC filings apart from land records, so land record fees cover them.

sections.h2: What are the recording charges for an Oakland County deed?
sections.html:
One deed carries a flat $30 charge, whatever its length. That figure includes the $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee, and Michigan's fee statute, MCL 600.2567, sets the same $30 base amount.

Oakland County Register of Deeds fees and transfer tax rates
ItemCharge
Entering a deed, mortgage or lis pendens$30.00
Added liber and page reference on a discharge or assignment$3.00
Photocopies, each page$1.00 per page
Certifying a copy$5.00 per document
Treasurer's tax certificate for warranty deeds$5.00
County transfer tax$0.55 per $500 of consideration
State transfer tax$3.75 per $500 of consideration

A deed carrying a warranty covenant, along with every land contract, needs the county treasurer's tax certification before it is recorded. If you mail a document in, the register will obtain the certificate and attach revenue stamps for you, and the $5 certificate fee goes into your payment.

sections.h2: How much does transfer tax add to an Oakland County sale?
sections.html:
Michigan taxes any written transfer of real property worth $100 or more. Oakland County's county share is $1.10 per $1,000 of consideration, and the state share is $7.50 per $1,000. Where an exemption applies, the reason has to be printed on the document itself.

Take the county's $343,600 median owner-occupied value as an example. County tax would be about $378 and state tax about $2,577, so roughly $2,955 in all. Michigan's two transfer tax acts, as summarized by the Oceana County register, place the tax on the seller or grantor, so plan for it on the seller's side of the closing statement.

  • Show the total value of the property on the deed, or attach an affidavit giving it.
  • Print any claimed exemption on the document.
  • Ask the title company how the stamps will be purchased and paid at closing.

sections.h2: What must an Oakland County document contain before it can be recorded?
sections.html:
The register accepts a document when it satisfies the format and signature rules in Michigan's recording statute, MCL 565.201. Staff examine each one and record only those that pass, and a validation unit checks the legal description before the cashier takes the document.

  • Signatures are original, with the signer's name typed or printed below.
  • The names in the notary block match the names under the signatures.
  • Any instrument that conveys or encumbers real estate shows the grantee's name and address.
  • A document signed in Michigan carries a notary acknowledgment listing the notary's county of commission and expiration date.
  • Black ink, type of at least 10 points, and white paper of 20-pound weight, sized from letter to legal length.
  • An unprinted band of 2.5 inches opens the first page, with half an inch left clear elsewhere.
  • The first printed line names the recordable event.
  • The property's full value appears on the face or in an attached affidavit.

A document naming a survivor needs a certified death certificate or proof of death. Court orders must be certified and sealed by the court clerk. Older instruments follow the rules of their day: male grantors' marital status was required before April 6, 2017, and two witnesses before March 2002.

sections.h2: Can Oakland County documents be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, the register accepts e-recording through registered providers, including Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and HopDox. UCC documents and mortgage foreclosure documents cannot be e-recorded.

The county also runs MiPropDocs for documents that do not transfer ownership. It accepts affidavits, association liens and discharges, claims of lien, certificates of trust, discharges, lis pendens, mortgages, notices of commencement, releases and satisfactions of mortgage. A deed cannot go through it, so an owner transferring a house still needs a title company e-recording account or a paper filing.

Paper filings remain open to anyone. Hand-carry the original to the counter or mail it with the fee, and keep the legal description exactly as it appears on the prior deed so the validation step does not send the document back.

sections.h2: How do the register and the county treasurer work together on a sale?
sections.html:
The two offices meet at the tax certificate. Before a warranty deed is recorded, the treasurer confirms that the parcel's taxes are paid up, and the register will not file the deed without that stamp. Delinquent balances can be priced beforehand: owners and title companies buy an official delinquent tax statement from the county's Property Gateway.

The register also touches tax foreclosure at the end of the line. It collects redemption money for sheriff deeds and clerk deeds, checks that the person redeeming has an interest in the property, and passes the funds to the treasurer, who holds them in trust until the paperwork is finished and a check can go to the grantee. A seller who inherited a house with unpaid taxes should read the Oakland County property tax guide before listing, since the county's foreclosure calendar runs on fixed dates.

sections.h2: How soon does a recorded deed come back?
sections.html:
Expect about two weeks for a document hand-carried to the counter and about two to four weeks for one sent by mail. A document that came through a title company usually returns about two weeks after recording. The register indexes and returns recorded originals by U.S. Mail unless a pickup was arranged.

Copy requests move faster. Walk-in customers get five pages as a courtesy, and larger orders are usually finished within 24 to 48 hours, with pickup in person or by mail. The office will also give a payoff figure for a foreclosure and handles redemptions on sheriff deeds and clerk deeds for people with an interest in the property. Money for a redemption is receipted and held by the treasurer until paperwork is complete.

faqs.q: How much is the Oakland County recording fee?
faqs.a: $30 per document, with no charge for extra pages. The amount already contains the $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee. A discharge covering several instruments adds $3.00 for each additional reference.

faqs.q: Is a tax certificate required for a warranty deed in Oakland County?
faqs.a: Yes. Warranty deeds, land contracts and deeds with a warranty clause need certification from the Oakland County Treasurer's Office, at $5.00, before the register will record them.

faqs.q: How far back do the county's online records reach?
faqs.a: To January 1, 1964, apart from subdivision plat maps. For anything earlier, contact the Register of Deeds at 248-858-0597.

faqs.q: Are UCC statements still filed separately in Oakland County?
faqs.a: No. After November 3, 2025 they are handled with land records, and land record recording fees apply.

faqs.q: Which party owes transfer tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: The seller or grantor, under the Michigan acts, due when the deed is recorded. County and state tax together come to about $8.60 per $1,000 of price in Oakland County.
